A debugger that uses the same interface as the code editor, so you can debug using the same environment that you use to write your code. 

Historically, debuggers were separate programs that had command-line interfaces. Later, debuggers were still separate, but supplied a graphical front end to make working with them easier.

While integrated debuggers are highly convenient and recommended for beginners, command line debuggers are well supported and still commonly used in environments that do not support graphical interfaces (e.g. embedded systems).
